newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lack of EU reform bad for bloc's future -- Santer.
newsitem.headline: Lack of EU reform bad for bloc's future -- Santer.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer condemned on Thursday the failure of European Union leaders at last week's Amsterdam summit sufficiently to reform the EU bloc in time for enlargement eastwards.
"I do not think this augurs well for enlargement," Santer told the European Parliament which delivered its own barrage of criticism at the lack of internal reform.

"I do not want to see a sitution whereby on the eve of enlargement we are forced to say to our future members: 'You have done everything to prepare yourselves for entering the EU. Unfortunately the EU hasn't been able to get ready to receive you'," Santer said.
He was speaking as EU foreign ministers were meeting in Luxembourg to approve a legal version of the new EU treaty clinched in Amsterdam, which will be formally signed in October.
The Amsterdam summit failed to bring about hoped-for reforms to the EU institutions -- originally designed for a bloc of six members -- in preparation for a Union of up to 25 members.

EU leaders could not agree to increase substantially the areas of policy where measures can be approved by a qualified majority of the 15 member states, thus limiting the ability of individual countries to block them.
They also failed to limit the number of commissioners EU states can appoint to Brussels or change nations' voting rights.
They proposed instead that institutional issues should be revisited at the time of the next EU expansion, due around 2002.
Santer condemned this result as "mediocre", an accusation acknowledged by Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, whose country holds the EU presidency.

The Commission President conceded that some progress had been made at Amsterdam which would allow the EU to act on jobs, fraud, crime and the environment, and to improve working conditions, freedom of movement and equal pay for men and women.
But he said the negotiations had been particularly difficult because they had dealt with extremely sensitive issues.

And on areas like decision-making powers, foreign and defence policy and trade the talks had also been frustrating and marred by "a certain lack of political will and a certain worrying tendency to give priority to purely national points of view," Santer contined.
"We will have to show more political will when the time (for enlargement to eastern Europe) comes," he warned.
Parliament later adopted a resolution demanding new internal EU reforms before any further enlargement, echoing a call made on Wednesday by Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene.
